grammarNotes.title: Telling the time: full hours
grammarNotes.body:
Ask **Wie spät ist es?** or **Wie viel Uhr ist es?** Answer with **Es ist … Uhr.**

- One o'clock is **ein Uhr**, not *eins Uhr*. Without *Uhr* it's *Es ist eins.*
- **um** + time = *at*: *um acht Uhr* = at eight o'clock. To ask *At what time?*, say **Um wie viel Uhr?**
- **Uhr** is a time on the clock, **Stunde** is an amount of time: *drei Uhr* = three o'clock, *drei Stunden* = three hours.

Timetables, shops and the radio use the 24-hour clock, with *Uhr* in the middle: *15:30* = **fünfzehn Uhr dreißig**, *8:10* = **acht Uhr zehn**.

grammarNotes.title: halb, Viertel, nach and vor
grammarNotes.body:
**halb** looks *forward* to the next hour: **halb vier** means halfway to four, so it's **3:30**, not 4:30. Always think one hour ahead: *halb acht* = 7:30, *halb eins* = 12:30.

**Viertel nach** (quarter past) and **Viertel vor** (quarter to) work just like English. Minutes use **nach** and **vor** too: *zehn nach zwei* = 2:10, *zehn vor zwei* = 1:50.

With *halb*, *Viertel*, *nach* and *vor*, leave out *Uhr*: *Es ist halb vier.*

Near the half hour you'll also hear times counted from *halb*: *fünf vor halb vier* = 3:25, *fünf nach halb vier* = 3:35.

grammarNotes.title: Separable verbs
grammarNotes.body:
Verbs like **aufstehen** have a small prefix that splits off. In a normal sentence, the verb goes **second** as usual and the prefix jumps to the **very end**:

- *aufstehen* → Ich **stehe** um sieben Uhr **auf**.
- *anrufen* → Ich **rufe** meine Mutter **an**.

When the verb is in its dictionary form, it stays in one piece, for example after *möchten*: *Ich möchte **fernsehen**.*

The stress is always on the prefix: **AUF**stehen, **AN**rufen, **FERN**sehen.
table: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
Der Film fängt um acht Uhr an.
Ich kaufe um fünf Uhr ein.

grammarNotes.title: Time first, verb second
grammarNotes.body:
In a German statement, the verb is always the **second** item. Usually the subject comes first, but you can start with a time instead. Then the subject moves to just **after** the verb:

- *Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.*
- *Um sieben Uhr stehe ich auf.*
- *Morgens trinke ich Kaffee.*
- *Zuerst frühstücke ich, dann gehe ich zur Arbeit.*

Second means the second *item*, not the second word: *um sieben Uhr* counts as one item. You'll practise this more in Unit 9.

grammarNotes.title: schlafen, anfangen, fernsehen: vowel changes
grammarNotes.body:
Like *sprechen* and *essen*, some verbs change their vowel in the **du** and **er/sie/es** forms only:

- **a → ä**: *schlafen → du schläfst*, *anfangen → er fängt an*
- **e → ie**: *fernsehen → sie sieht fern*

All the other forms are regular.

exercises.title: Wie spät ist es?
exercises.body:
To ask the time, say **Wie spät ist es?** (literally *How late is it?*). You'll also hear **Wie viel Uhr ist es?** Both mean *What time is it?*

For full hours, answer **Es ist … Uhr.** with the numbers you already know. **die Uhr** is the clock, and in times it means *o'clock*.

exercises.title: ein Uhr, not eins Uhr
exercises.body:
One small trap: right before **Uhr**, *eins* loses its *s*: **Es ist ein Uhr.**

In everyday speech people often drop *Uhr* altogether. Then *eins* keeps its *s*: **Es ist eins.**

accepted: ein
exercises.translation: It's one o'clock.
Excuse me, what time is it?

exercises.title: um: at
exercises.body:
**um** + a time = *at* that time:

- *Es ist acht Uhr.* It's eight o'clock.
- *Ich lerne **um** acht Uhr Deutsch.* I study German at eight o'clock.

To ask *At what time?*, say **Um wie viel Uhr?**

alternatives: Ich lerne Deutsch um acht Uhr.

exercises.title: Stunde and Minute
exercises.body:
- **die Stunde** = the hour, plural **Stunden**
- **die Minute** = the minute, plural **Minuten**

Don't mix up *Uhr* and *Stunde*. **Uhr** is a time on the clock: *drei Uhr* = three o'clock. **Stunde** is an amount of time: *drei Stunden* = three hours.

exercises.title: halb: the big trap
exercises.body:
This one catches every English speaker:

**halb vier** does *not* mean half past four. It means **half past three** (3:30).

German counts *towards* the next hour: *halb vier* = halfway to four. So always think one hour **ahead**:

- 3:30 = **halb vier**
- 7:30 = **halb acht**
- 12:30 = **halb eins**

There's no *Uhr* here: *Es ist halb vier.*

examples.hint: without Uhr, eins keeps its s

exercises.instruction: What time is it? Remember: think one hour ahead.

exercises.title: Viertel nach, Viertel vor
exercises.body:
**das Viertel** = the quarter. *Viertel* starts with an *f* sound, just like *vier*.

- **nach** = past: *Viertel nach drei* = 3:15
- **vor** = to: *Viertel vor vier* = 3:45

These work just like English *quarter past* and *quarter to*. No trap this time!

accepted: nach
exercises.translation: It's quarter past eight.

exercises.title: Five past, ten to
exercises.body:
Minutes work the same way: number + **nach** or **vor** + hour.

- *fünf nach sechs* = 6:05
- *zwanzig nach sechs* = 6:20
- *zehn vor sieben* = 6:50

People usually leave out *Minuten* here, just as English drops *minutes* in *ten past six*.

exercises.title: Separable verbs
exercises.body:
Some German verbs come in two parts: a small **prefix** and a verb. **aufstehen** (to get up) is *auf* + *stehen*.

In a normal sentence the verb splits. The main part goes second, as usual, and the **prefix jumps to the very end**:

- *aufstehen* → Ich **stehe** um sieben Uhr **auf**.

The stress is always on the prefix: **AUF**stehen.

exercises.title: More separable verbs
exercises.body:
These all split the same way, and the prefix is always stressed:

- **AN**fangen = to start
- **EIN**kaufen = to go shopping
- **AN**rufen = to call (on the phone)
- **FERN**sehen = to watch TV

One thing to watch: **anfangen** changes *a* to *ä* with *er/sie/es*: *Der Film **fängt** um acht Uhr **an**.*

exercises.title: Starting with the time
exercises.body:
You can also start a sentence with the time. The verb stays in **second place**, so *ich* moves to just after it:

- *Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.*
- ***Um sieben Uhr** stehe ich auf.*

Both mean the same. The prefix stays at the end either way. You'll practise this more in Unit 9.

exercises.title: immer: always
exercises.body:
**immer** = always. Put it right after the verb:

- *Ich stehe **immer** um sechs Uhr auf.*
- *Wir sehen **immer** um acht Uhr fern.*

exercises.title: Three meals
exercises.body:
All three meals are *das* words:

- **das Frühstück** = breakfast
- **das Mittagessen** = lunch (*Mittag* = midday + *Essen* = food)
- **das Abendessen** = dinner (*Abend* = evening + *Essen*)

A compound word always takes the article of its **last** part: *das Essen*, so *das Mittagessen*.

examples.text: Das Frühstück ist um acht Uhr.

exercises.instruction: der, die or das? Look at the last part of the word.

exercises.title: frühstücken and kochen
exercises.body:
- **frühstücken** = to have breakfast. It's one word that never splits: *Ich frühstücke um sieben Uhr.*
- **kochen** = to cook, a regular verb: *ich koche, du kochst, er kocht*

examples.translation: I have breakfast at seven o'clock.

accepted: kocht
exercises.translation: He's cooking lunch.

exercises.title: morgens, mittags, abends
exercises.body:
Add **-s** to a part of the day and you get *in the …*, usually as a habit:

- **morgens** = in the morning
- **mittags** = at midday
- **abends** = in the evening

They come from *Morgen*, *Mittag* and *Abend* (as in *Guten Morgen*), but they're not nouns, so they're written in lowercase.

Start a sentence with one and the verb still comes **second**: *Morgens **trinke** ich Kaffee.*

examples.translation: In the morning I drink coffee.
At midday I eat a bread roll.
In the evening I watch TV.

exercises.translation: In the evening I cook dinner.

exercises.title: schlafen: a changes to ä
exercises.body:
**schlafen** = to sleep. Like *anfangen*, it changes **a** to **ä** in the *du* and *er/sie/es* forms:

- ich schlafe
- du **schläfst**
- er / sie **schläft**
- wir / sie / Sie schlafen

*fernsehen* changes too, *e* to *ie*: *Er **sieht** abends **fern**.*

accepted: schläft

exercises.title: Work and going
exercises.body:
- **arbeiten** = to work. The stem *arbeit-* ends in *-t*, so add an extra **e** to make it easy to say: du arbeit**e**st, er arbeit**e**t.
- **die Arbeit** = work, the job
- **gehen** = to go, a regular verb: ich gehe, du gehst, er geht

Two handy chunks to learn whole: **zur Arbeit gehen** = to go to work, **ins Bett gehen** = to go to bed.

exercises.title: zuerst, dann, später
exercises.body:
Tell your day in order:

- **zuerst** = first
- **dann** = then
- **später** = later

They work like a time: put one first and the verb comes **second**. *Zuerst **stehe** ich auf. Dann **frühstücke** ich.*

And when you leave: **Bis später!** = See you later!

examples.text: Zuerst stehe ich auf, dann frühstücke ich.
examples.translation: First I get up, then I have breakfast.
